data.name: Ahtsham
data.gender_notes: Ahtsham is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who protects his garden, or the one who takes care of the garden of knowledge. The name Ahtsham carries the meaning “Gardener, Protector” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Ahtsham usually hope their child will grow to embody gardener, protector and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Ahtsham belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gardener, Protector.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ahtsham total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_english.name: Ahtsham
in_english.long_meaning: The name Ahtsham is derived from the Arabic root 'حشم' (h-sh-m), which means to conceal or to have dignity. In Islamic tradition, Ahtsham signifies a person with dignified and honorable characteristics. The Quran references the importance of dignity and modesty, making this name a meaningful choice for Muslim parents.

In the context of the Islamic world, the term "garden" symbolizes knowledge, wisdom, and the overall betterment of oneself and society. Naming a child Ahtsham reinforces the idea that their role in society is to protect and care for the intellectual and moral growth of their community.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Ahtsham lies in its connection to the concept of stewardship and personal responsibility in Islamic teachings. Just as a gardener tenderly nurtures his plants to ensure their growth and development, a person with the name Ahtsham is seen as a steward of the Divine gifts bestowed upon them. The name Ahtsham encourages the bearer to take care of their own spiritual growth and to contribute to the betterment of their community, in line with the broader Islamic principle of being a good servant to God and His creation.
